summary: Bikoro territory (Equateur), on Lake Tumba south of Mbandaka, has no reported armed-group presence as of late 2026. The state exercises control through the territorial administration and the Congolese National Police (PNC), with Bikoro town as the territorial seat. Historic violence consists of localised land and intercommunal disputes rather than organised armed groups. All locations in the Bikoro, Iboko and Ntondo secteurs are assessed as default PNC control, with lower confidence for remote Iboko and Ntondo.

sources.title: CCAPS armed conflict location record (Bikoro land clash, Jan 2012)

zones.description: Bikoro town (territorial headquarters on Lake Tumba, incl. Cite A/B/C, Plateau, Bankome etc.)
zones.evidence: Bikoro is the seat of the territorial administration with a PNC territorial commissariat; Searches (FR/EN, 2025-2026) found no reports of armed groups, militias or rebel activity in Bikoro town; the only conflict events on record for Bikoro are localised land/intercommunal clashes (e.g. Jan 2012) handled by state forces. Western Equateur lies far from eastern conflict zones and the Mobondo militia area (Kwamouth/Kwango/Kwilu); state authority via territorial administration and PNC is assumed.
